ac.reason: Matched routing retains cache bypass. Hits require current objective, authority, callable-source, lifecycle and dependency checks followed by reconstruction using current inputs. Both hot and cold paths prohibit unconditional verbatim emission.

Semantic rejection uses live discovery and existing stale-miss handling. Missing-guide, unavailable-helper and non-checkout safeguards remain explicit. Insertion, evaluation and telemetry have eligibility/success guards. Cache/dispatch implementations are unchanged against Q0, preserving existing source hashes, guide invalidation, budgets and miss handling.

The ten existing keys are retained and pinned. Ordinary multi-file planning and workflow resume become unknown rather than forced MDTM. Raw generation, populated-document derivation and roadmap artifacts are distinguished. Cache/dispatch fixtures now pair spec-panel with adversarial-review while retaining round-trip, hash, budget and dispatch assertions.

Cold-worker policy agrees with the main verification and request-binding rules, but the required concrete negative consumer cases are missing. Added tests check generic wording rather than distinguish comparison versus adherence/PR review, PRD versus TDD/critique, roadmap/MDTM versus Sprint artifacts, changed request paths, dependency-only changes or hash-valid retired candidates.

findings.issue: The hot-consumer test does not require the incompatible/retired/unavailable/contradictory rejection branch or its live-discovery action. Its miss_validation_stale assertion can be satisfied by the ordinary miss list even if the semantic-rejection instruction is removed. This leaves required negative consumer coverage absent despite the correct production prose.

Preserve the existing runtime API/schema; do not describe static checks as model-generation proof.
